# Overview

This notebook extracts PICRUSt2-ready files from a saved `phyloseq` object.

It writes:

- `feature_table.biom` — raw feature/ASV count table in BIOM format
- `feature_table.tsv` — human-readable feature count table
- `study_seqs.fasta` — representative sequences
- `sample_metadata.tsv` — sample metadata, when available
- `taxonomy.tsv` — taxonomy table, when available
- `feature_id_map.tsv` — mapping between original taxa names and output feature IDs
- `prep_summary.tsv` — basic QC summary

> **Important:** PICRUSt2 requires representative sequences in FASTA format, not raw sequencing FASTQ files. Raw FASTQ reads are generally not stored in a `phyloseq` object and cannot be reconstructed from it.

This notebook supports two common phyloseq structures:

1. Representative sequences are stored in `refseq(physeq)`.
2. The ASV nucleotide sequences themselves are used as the taxa names, as is common in DADA2 workflows.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = TRUE,
  warning = TRUE
)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(phyloseq)
  library(biomformat)
  library(here)
})

phyloseq_rds <- params$phyloseq_rds
outdir <- params$outdir
rename_sequence_taxa <- params$rename_sequence_taxa

dir.create(
  outdir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

message("phyloseq object: ", phyloseq_rds)
message("Output directory: ", outdir)
```

# Load the phyloseq object

```{r load-phyloseq}
physeq <- readRDS(file = here("data/phyloseq/ps_all_css.rds"))

physeq
```

# Extract the raw count matrix

PICRUSt2 should receive the original feature counts rather than relative abundance, CLR, CPM, percentages, or other normalized values.

`phyloseq` objects can store taxa either as rows or columns. This chunk automatically converts the matrix to:

**features × samples**

```{r extract-count-matrix}
otu <- otu_table(physeq)

count_matrix <- as(
  otu,
  "matrix"
)

if (!taxa_are_rows(physeq)) {
  count_matrix <- t(count_matrix)
}

storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"

message(
  "Count matrix dimensions: ",
  nrow(count_matrix),
  " features x ",
  ncol(count_matrix),
  " samples"
)

if (anyNA(count_matrix)) {
  stop("Count matrix contains NA values.")
}

if (any(!is.finite(count_matrix))) {
  stop("Count matrix contains non-finite values.")
}

if (any(count_matrix < 0)) {
  stop("Count matrix contains negative values.")
}

if (!all(abs(count_matrix - round(count_matrix)) < 1e-8)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The phyloseq abundance table contains non-integer values. ",
      "PICRUSt2 should normally be run on raw ASV/OTU counts."
    )
  )
}

count_matrix <- round(count_matrix)
storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "integer"
```

# Remove zero-abundance features

```{r remove-zero-features}
zero_features <- rowSums(count_matrix) == 0

n_zero_features <- sum(zero_features)

if (n_zero_features > 0) {
  message(
    "Removing ",
    n_zero_features,
    " features with zero total abundance."
  )

  count_matrix <- count_matrix[
    !zero_features,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
}

if (nrow(count_matrix) == 0) {
  stop("No non-zero features remain.")
}
```

# Extract representative sequences

First, the notebook checks whether representative sequences are stored in the phyloseq `refseq` component.

If not, it checks whether the taxa names themselves look like nucleotide sequences.

```{r extract-representative-sequences}
original_feature_ids <- rownames(count_matrix)

ref_sequences <- NULL
sequence_source <- NULL

# Try phyloseq refseq first.
refseq_object <- tryCatch(
  phyloseq::refseq(physeq),
  error = function(e) NULL
)

if (!is.null(refseq_object)) {

  ref_sequences <- as.character(refseq_object)

  if (is.null(names(ref_sequences))) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "A refseq component was found, but its sequences do not have names. ",
        "The sequence names must correspond to phyloseq taxa IDs."
      )
    )
  }

  sequence_source <- "phyloseq refseq"

} else {

  taxa_ids <- taxa_names(physeq)

  looks_like_dna <- grepl(
    "^[ACGTURYKMSWBDHVNacgturykmswbdhvn-]+$",
    taxa_ids
  )

  sufficiently_long <- nchar(taxa_ids) >= 20

  if (all(looks_like_dna & sufficiently_long)) {

    ref_sequences <- toupper(taxa_ids)
    names(ref_sequences) <- taxa_ids
    sequence_source <- "taxa names"

  } else {

    stop(
      paste0(
        "\nNo representative sequences were found in the phyloseq object.\n\n",
        "The object has no usable refseq component and the taxa names do not ",
        "appear to be nucleotide sequences.\n\n",
        "Raw FASTQ files cannot be reconstructed from a phyloseq object. ",
        "You will need the representative ASV/OTU FASTA from the upstream ",
        "DADA2/QIIME2/mothur processing workflow."
      )
    )
  }
}

message("Representative sequence source: ", sequence_source)
message("Sequences available: ", length(ref_sequences))
```

# Match count-table features and sequences

```{r match-features}
features_with_sequence <- intersect(
  rownames(count_matrix),
  names(ref_sequences)
)

features_missing_sequence <- setdiff(
  rownames(count_matrix),
  names(ref_sequences)
)

sequences_missing_counts <- setdiff(
  names(ref_sequences),
  rownames(count_matrix)
)

message("Features in count matrix: ", nrow(count_matrix))
message("Features with representative sequence: ", length(features_with_sequence))
message("Features lacking a sequence: ", length(features_missing_sequence))
message("Sequences lacking counts: ", length(sequences_missing_counts))

if (length(features_with_sequence) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No feature IDs overlap between the count matrix and representative sequences."
  )
}

writeLines(
  features_missing_sequence,
  file.path(outdir, "features_missing_sequence.txt")
)

writeLines(
  sequences_missing_counts,
  file.path(outdir, "sequences_missing_counts.txt")
)

count_matrix <- count_matrix[
  features_with_sequence,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

ref_sequences <- ref_sequences[
  features_with_sequence
]
```

# Assign simple ASV IDs when appropriate

When DADA2 sequences are stored directly as taxa names, PICRUSt2 can technically use those sequences as IDs, but simple IDs such as `ASV1`, `ASV2`, etc. make downstream files much easier to work with.

Set the YAML parameter:

```text
rename_sequence_taxa: false
```

if you want to keep the original taxa names unchanged.

```{r feature-ids}
old_ids <- rownames(count_matrix)

ids_are_sequences <- grepl(
  "^[ACGTURYKMSWBDHVNacgturykmswbdhvn-]+$",
  old_ids
) & nchar(old_ids) >= 20

if (rename_sequence_taxa && all(ids_are_sequences)) {

  new_ids <- paste0(
    "ASV",
    seq_len(nrow(count_matrix))
  )

} else {

  new_ids <- old_ids
}

feature_id_map <- data.frame(
  feature_id = new_ids,
  original_taxon_id = old_ids,
  sequence = unname(ref_sequences),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

rownames(count_matrix) <- new_ids
names(ref_sequences) <- new_ids

write.table(
  feature_id_map,
  file = file.path(outdir, "feature_id_map.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

head(feature_id_map)
```

# Remove zero-read samples after matching

```{r remove-zero-samples}
zero_samples <- colSums(count_matrix) == 0

if (any(zero_samples)) {

  message(
    "Removing ",
    sum(zero_samples),
    " samples with zero reads after feature matching."
  )

  message(
    paste(
      colnames(count_matrix)[zero_samples],
      collapse = "\n"
    )
  )

  count_matrix <- count_matrix[
    ,
    !zero_samples,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
}

if (ncol(count_matrix) == 0) {
  stop("No samples remain after filtering.")
}
```

# Write the count table as TSV

```{r write-count-tsv}
feature_table_tsv <- data.frame(
  FeatureID = rownames(count_matrix),
  count_matrix,
  check.names = FALSE
)

write.table(
  feature_table_tsv,
  file = file.path(outdir, "feature_table.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

message(
  "Saved: ",
  file.path(outdir, "feature_table.tsv")
)
```

# Write the BIOM count table

```{r write-biom}
biom_object <- make_biom(
  data = count_matrix
)

biom_file <- file.path(
  outdir,
  "feature_table.biom"
)

write_biom(
  biom_object,
  biom_file
)

message("Saved: ", biom_file)
```

# Validate the BIOM file

```{r validate-biom}
biom_check <- read_biom(
  biom_file
)

biom_check_matrix <- as.matrix(
  biom_data(biom_check)
)

if (!identical(
  rownames(biom_check_matrix),
  rownames(count_matrix)
)) {
  stop("BIOM validation failed: feature IDs changed.")
}

if (!identical(
  colnames(biom_check_matrix),
  colnames(count_matrix)
)) {
  stop("BIOM validation failed: sample IDs changed.")
}

message("BIOM validation passed.")
```

# Write representative sequences as FASTA

PICRUSt2 expects the FASTA header for each sequence to contain only the corresponding feature ID.

```{r write-fasta}
fasta_file <- file.path(
  outdir,
  "study_seqs.fasta"
)

con <- file(
  fasta_file,
  open = "wt"
)

for (feature_id in names(ref_sequences)) {

  sequence <- ref_sequences[[feature_id]]

  writeLines(
    paste0(">", feature_id),
    con
  )

  sequence_length <- nchar(sequence)

  starts <- seq(
    1,
    sequence_length,
    by = 80
  )

  ends <- pmin(
    starts + 79,
    sequence_length
  )

  wrapped_sequence <- substring(
    sequence,
    starts,
    ends
  )

  writeLines(
    wrapped_sequence,
    con
  )
}

close(con)

message("Saved: ", fasta_file)
```

# Export sample metadata

```{r sample-metadata}
sample_data_object <- tryCatch(
  sample_data(physeq),
  error = function(e) NULL
)

if (!is.null(sample_data_object)) {

  metadata <- as.data.frame(
    sample_data_object,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  metadata <- metadata[
    colnames(count_matrix),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  metadata <- data.frame(
    SampleID = rownames(metadata),
    metadata,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  write.table(
    metadata,
    file = file.path(outdir, "sample_metadata.tsv"),
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  message(
    "Saved: ",
    file.path(outdir, "sample_metadata.tsv")
  )
}
```

# Export taxonomy

Taxonomy is not required for the main PICRUSt2 prediction pipeline, but it is useful to retain for interpretation and QC.

```{r taxonomy}
tax_object <- tryCatch(
  tax_table(physeq),
  error = function(e) NULL
)

if (!is.null(tax_object)) {

  taxonomy_matrix <- as(
    tax_object,
    "matrix"
  )

  taxonomy_matrix <- taxonomy_matrix[
    old_ids,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  taxonomy_df <- data.frame(
    FeatureID = new_ids,
    taxonomy_matrix,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  write.table(
    taxonomy_df,
    file = file.path(outdir, "taxonomy.tsv"),
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  message(
    "Saved: ",
    file.path(outdir, "taxonomy.tsv")
  )
}
```

# QC summary

```{r qc-summary}
summary_df <- data.frame(
  metric = c(
    "sequence_source",
    "final_features",
    "final_samples",
    "total_reads",
    "minimum_sample_reads",
    "median_sample_reads",
    "maximum_sample_reads",
    "features_missing_sequence",
    "sequences_missing_counts"
  ),
  value = c(
    sequence_source,
    nrow(count_matrix),
    ncol(count_matrix),
    sum(count_matrix),
    min(colSums(count_matrix)),
    median(colSums(count_matrix)),
    max(colSums(count_matrix)),
    length(features_missing_sequence),
    length(sequences_missing_counts)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

write.table(
  summary_df,
  file = file.path(outdir, "prep_summary.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

summary_df
```

# Final PICRUSt2 inputs

The two files needed for PICRUSt2 are:

```text
picrust2_input/feature_table.biom
picrust2_input/study_seqs.fasta
```

A typical PICRUSt2 command is:

```bash
picrust2_pipeline.py \
    -s picrust2_input/study_seqs.fasta \
    -i picrust2_input/feature_table.biom \
    -o picrust2_output \
    -p 8
```

Before running PICRUSt2, the BIOM file can also be checked from the command line:

```bash
biom summarize-table \
    -i picrust2_input/feature_table.biom

biom validate-table \
    -i picrust2_input/feature_table.biom
```
